name: MonarchUsageMeter
title: UsageMeter
wrapsNative: ProgressView with a ProgressViewStyle per item
summary: Usage against limits: for each metered item, what was used, the limit and a meter that turns to the warning colour near the limit and the danger colour over it, with the level written as text.
whenToUse: On a billing or plan screen, to show requests, storage, seats or minutes used in a period.
whenNotToUse: For the progress of a task, use ProgressView with the Monarch linear style. For one reading against a scale, use MonarchGauge.
api: MonarchUsageMeter.init(_ title: String? = nil, items: [MonarchUsageMeterItem], period: String? = nil, resetsAt: Date? = nil, warningAt: Double = 0.8, isLoading: Bool = false, error: String? = nil, isRetrying: Bool = false, labels: MonarchUsageMeterLabels = MonarchUsageMeterLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchUsageMeterItem.init(_ label: String, id: String? = nil, used: Double, limit: Double? = nil, unit: String? = nil, description: String? = nil)

MonarchUsageMeterLabels.init(amount: (@Sendable (_ used: String, _ limit: String) -> String)? = nil, percent: (@Sendable (_ percent: String) -> String)? = nil, nearLimit: String? = nil, overLimit: String? = nil, resets: (@Sendable (_ date: String) -> String)? = nil, announcement: (@Sendable (_ label: String, _ level: String) -> String)? = nil, loading: String? = nil, retry: String? = nil)

options.name: items
options.description: The metered items, in display order. An item without a limit shows the count alone.

options.name: period
options.description: The period measured, such as "This month".

options.name: resetsAt
options.description: When the quota resets. Written in the locale and time zone of the environment.

options.name: warningAt
options.description: The fraction of the limit at which an item is near the limit.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows redacted placeholder rows, as many as items or three, instead of the items. VoiceOver reads "Loading usage".

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, shown instead of the items.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: Whether a retry is running. The retry button waits and reads Retrying.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces any of the built-in strings.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a "Try again" button under the error.

states.name: normal
states.description: The meter is filled in the accent colour and the line under it reads "42% used".

states.name: near the limit
states.description: At or above warningAt: the warning colour, a warning icon and "Near the limit · 84% used".

states.name: over the limit
states.description: Above the limit: a full meter in the danger colour, a danger icon and "Over the limit · 130% used".

states.name: unlimited
states.description: No limit, or a limit of zero or less: the count and the unit, with no meter.

states.name: loading
states.description: Redacted placeholder rows replace the items and are read as one Loading usage element.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry replaces the items when onRetry is given, a plain error notice when not.

appearance: A muted track with a fill in the accent, warning or danger solid colour. The status line uses the matching strong colour and an icon; labels and descriptions are muted text, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web component lays items out in a grid or a list; on a phone they are a single column, so there is no layout option. Like the web, loading draws skeleton rows and the error uses MonarchInlineErrorRetry. The web has header actions, a heading level, compact notation and a per-item formatter; these are not offered: numbers use the locale of the environment with at most one fraction digit. The eight built-in strings are replaced through MonarchUsageMeterLabels rather than one parameter each. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
Each item is one element: its label is the item's label and its value is the figures, the level and the percentage, for example "42 of 50 GB, Near the limit, 84% used".
Near and over the limit are written as text and have an icon, so they do not depend on the colour of the meter.
When the level of an item changes while the view is on screen, VoiceOver announces every item that is near or over its limit.
The placeholder rows are read as one Loading usage element.
The retry button is the one of MonarchInlineErrorRetry, with a 44-point touch target.
All text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps.
edgeCases: Used above the limit draws a full meter; the percentage shows the real share, such as 130%.
Exactly at the limit is near the limit, not over it.
A limit of zero, a negative limit or a limit that is not a number is treated as no limit.
The error takes precedence over loading.
The announcement is posted when levels change, not when the view first appears.
The unit is written after the figures with a space, in every locale.

examples.title: Quotas and counts
examples.template:
MonarchUsageMeter(
    {{title}},
    items: [
        MonarchUsageMeterItem({{items.0.label}}, id: {{items.0.id}}, used: {{items.0.used}}, limit: {{items.0.limit}}),
        MonarchUsageMeterItem({{items.1.label}}, id: {{items.1.id}}, used: {{items.1.used}}, limit: {{items.1.limit}}),
        MonarchUsageMeterItem({{items.2.label}}, id: {{items.2.id}}, used: {{items.2.used}}, limit: {{items.2.limit}}, unit: {{items.2.unit}}),
        MonarchUsageMeterItem({{items.3.label}}, id: {{items.3.id}}, used: {{items.3.used}}, description: {{items.3.description}}),
    ],
    period: {{period}},
    resetsAt: {{resetsAt|date}}
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: {{locale}}))
.environment(\.timeZone, TimeZone(identifier: {{timeZone}}) ?? .gmt)
examples.code:
MonarchUsageMeter(
    "Usage",
    items: [
        MonarchUsageMeterItem("Requests", id: "req", used: 4200, limit: 10_000),
        MonarchUsageMeterItem("Messages", id: "msg", used: 8500, limit: 10_000),
        MonarchUsageMeterItem("Storage", id: "gb", used: 12, limit: 10, unit: "GB"),
        MonarchUsageMeterItem("Conversations", id: "conv", used: 31, description: "Conversations started"),
    ],
    period: "This month",
    resetsAt: Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_796_083_200)
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en-GB"))
.environment(\.timeZone, TimeZone(identifier: "UTC") ?? .gmt)
